answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with graduated trust built from verifiable work history. A new identity starts in a harbor of low limits: it may handle only tiny, easily checked tasks. As it completes jobs honestly over weeks, its reputation rises like a mesa, layer by layer, unlocking larger work. Creating thousands of fake identities is cheap, but aging each one through real, auditable work is slow and costly, so an attacker cannot instantly flood the market. A Sybil swarm remains a dry oasis of empty accounts, while genuine agents carry a costly, checkable past.
